headline: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis
dek: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude helped produce a draft proof of the Riemann hypothesis, while Google replaces its desktop Search button with AI‑focused icons and a chat sidebar[S1][S2][S3].
what_happened: Levent Alpöge says Claude helped him draft a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, but the result is still unverified[S1].
Google’s desktop homepage now shows AI feature icons and a sidebar for recent AI chats, while the classic Search button is removed[S2][S3].

Apple is hiring a senior engineering manager to lead development of an AI agent that can operate a Mac, according to a job posting cited by Bloomberg and reported by TechCrunch on 20 November 2026[S4].

sections.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis
paragraphs: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced on his website that he believes he has proved the Riemann hypothesis using the large language model Claude[S1]. He said the proof was completed late Sunday night and that he delayed public release until after Anthropic’s IPO on Thursday[S1]. The claim has not been independently verified and Anthropic has not commented on the result[S1].

Alpöge’s proof was written in the Lean proof assistant and extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, with a suggestion it could also address the Extended Riemann Hypothesis given more time[S1]. The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, each carrying a $1 million prize from the Clay Mathematics Institute[S1]. Anthropic previously noted in August that it was experimenting with Claude on the problem but did not expect the model’s techniques to yield a proof[S1]. The claim remains a draft on Alpöge’s site and has not been submitted for formal acceptance by the Institute[S1].

The Riemann hypothesis, first proposed in 1859, concerns how the non‑trivial zeroes of the Riemann zeta function relate to the distribution of prime numbers, a central question in number theory[S1]. Solving it would be a historic breakthrough, as it has resisted proof by the world’s leading mathematicians for decades[S1].

sections.title: Google adds AI chat sidebar and removes search button
paragraphs: Google has replaced the traditional Search button on its desktop homepage with a set of AI‑focused icons and an expandable sidebar that shows recent AI Mode conversations[S2][S3]. The “I’m Feeling Lucky” button remains, but the classic Search button is gone[S2][S3].

The new homepage places three new icons under the query bar: one for image generation, one for file analysis, and one for brainstorming with Gemini, Google’s conversational model[S2][S3]. A gray bar on the left opens a collapsible sidebar that lists prior AI chats, lets users start a new thread, search past threads, or link a Gemini Notebook[S2][S3]. Stein said the sidebar made a “big difference” in how users continue web searches, describing it as a simpler way to pick up where they left off[S2][S3].
Google’s search interface has long featured a permanent Search button, but autocomplete suggestions often hide it, leading most users to press Enter instead[S2][S3].

The sidebar shows recent Gemini conversations, letting users resume searches instantly[S3].

sections.title: Apple works on AI agent for Mac computers
paragraphs: Apple is hiring a senior engineering manager to lead development of an AI agent that can operate a Mac, according to a job posting cited by Bloomberg and reported by TechCrunch on 20 November 2026[S4]. The agent is described as able to browse the web, run commands, write and debug code, and call services, all while choosing the appropriate tool for each step[S4]. Apple has not commented on the effort[S4].

The posting says the agent will move fluidly between apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, handling multi‑step tasks across these environments[S4]. Apple plans to roll out the feature in macOS 27.3, which will also add warnings to limit third‑party agents from gaining full system control[S4]. The company aims to introduce the service as early as the end of next year, though development is still in early stages[S4].

AI agents that can use a computer have become a hot commodity, with firms like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta launching similar services in the past year[S4]. Apple’s push aligns with its broader AI strategy under senior vice president John Ternus, seeking to expand its assistant capabilities while tightening security for third‑party tools[S4].

sections.title: Signal blocks screenshots to stop AI agents
paragraphs: The change targets built‑in agents such as Apple’s Siri and Google’s Gemini, which can capture on‑screen content for assistance[S5][S6]. Users can re‑enable screenshots in the app settings, but doing so may expose their chats to those agents[S5].

Signal’s president Meredith Whittaker said the AI agents are “hostile to privacy” and that existing OS tools do not let developers easily block data access without harming user experience[S5]. The screenshot block is a partial fix because AI agents can also read data from the device file system or via deep accessibility permissions used by third‑party tools like Meta’s Muse[S5]. Last year Signal used a similar block to stop Microsoft’s Recall feature from capturing secured chats on Windows 11, showing a pattern of defensive measures against AI‑driven snooping[S6]. The company is urging Apple, Google and Microsoft to provide simple technical controls and clear documentation for developers[S5].

Modern smartphones embed AI assistants that analyze screen content to answer user queries, a function that can inadvertently expose private messages[S5][S6]. Encrypted messaging apps like Signal rely on end‑to‑end encryption, but screen‑capture capabilities bypass that protection by sending visible text to remote servers[S6]. Without OS‑level opt‑out mechanisms, app developers have limited ways to safeguard against such AI‑driven data leakage[S5].

sections.title: Meta prices Muse Charm at $300
paragraphs: Meta announced that its Muse Charm wearable will cost $300 and is slated to ship before the December holidays[S8]. The device is a small gadget with a screen that lets users talk to the Muse AI agent using a fingerprint sensor[S8].

The Muse Charm bundles real‑time voice and avatar technology into a pocket‑sized device, according to CEO Mark Zuckerberg[S8]. It includes a fingerprint sensor that lets users activate the AI without unlocking a phone[S8]. The Information reports the device will include a free 12‑month 5G data plan from Verizon[S8]. Comparable AI wearables include Friend’s device at $250 and Amazon’s Bee Frontier at $75 (currently discounted to $52.49)[S7]. Meta has previously launched the Muse agent and a range of avatars for personalization[S7].
AI wearables have struggled to gain mass adoption, with earlier products like the Humane AI Pin receiving limited consumer uptake[S7].
